task_instance: Run a simulated Session 1 / Track A (Foundation) blueprint workshop for a fictitious client (Northwind Fabrications, a two-entity UK/Ireland manufacturer implementing D365 F&SCM), following the skill's five-beat process (Frame/Ask/Propose/Record/Draft-and-save) for sections 1-3, and produce the working blueprint markdown file with a progress tracker, a decision log (all six required fields per entry), an assumptions register, a constraints register, and an open-items register that correctly flags the unresolved deployment-phasing question as a load-bearing OPEN item with owner and date rather than inventing an answer.
evidence: Read SKILL.md at /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler/benchmark/ce_sources/github__awesome-copilot__d365-solution-blueprint/SKILL.md. Confirmed via `find` that the skill package only ships SKILL.md and LICENSE (references/section-guide.md and assets/blueprint-template.md, which the skill points to for detailed per-section question sets and a formatting template, are absent) -- handled per the skill's own fallback instruction ('If the file is absent, use the conventions in this skill as written'). Authored /tmp/claude-0/.../northwind-fabrications-solution-blueprint-v1.md (145 lines, verified with `wc -l`/`grep -c '^|'` = 51 table rows) containing: a control page; a progress tracker covering all 14 sections with status; a decision log with 3 entries each carrying Decision/Rationale/Alternatives rejected/Implications/Decided by/Date; an assumptions register (2 entries with owner + validation date); a constraints register (2 entries); an open items register correctly marking the deployment-phasing question (load-bearing decision #4 from the skill's list) as OPEN with an owner and needed-by date instead of assuming an answer; and full Frame/Ask/Propose/Record beats for sections 1-3 (Programme context, Scope, Target operating model), including an Architect's note where the architect's view differed from the sponsor's framing, and an explicit carry-forward of the skill's Microsoft-Learn verification-discipline obligation for later platform-capability claims. This demonstrates the skill's core deliverable -- a structured, decision-log-driven D365 Solution Blueprint document produced through the interview method described -- is producible as pure document authoring within this runtime, with no external tool, account, or network dependency required for the core task.
notes: Deliberately did not fabricate resolutions for the load-bearing phasing decision, in keeping with the skill's central failure-mode warning against inventing client answers. A full multi-session engagement (all 14 sections, live Microsoft Learn verification calls for platform-capability claims in Track B onward) was out of scope for a single ~15-minute representative instance, but the one completed track exercises the full mechanic (five-beat process, decision log discipline, load-bearing-item handling, progress tracker) that defines the skill's deliverable.
